pathFreeIsAStrengthening.why: The old test asked whether a candidate's ownership path string is a member of the in-flight path set. Ownership, though, is a directory claim: a unit that owns 'src/lib' owns every file beneath it, so a second unit admitted at 'src/lib/multiplayer/server' edits files the first unit already holds. The old test cannot see that, because the two strings differ. Containment on a directory boundary is the smallest rule that matches what ownership already means, and it is strictly narrower: every pair the old rule blocked (string equality) the new rule still blocks, and it additionally blocks the nested pairs. No unit that was admissible for a reason other than a nested path becomes inadmissible, so the validator gains a refusal and loses none. 'src/libx' stays unrelated to 'src/lib' because the rule requires the '/' boundary.

pathFreeIsAStrengthening.counterfactualThatIsolatesIt: Recomputing the same selection with U15a and U15b treated as main-verified (out of flight) and U4 still local-verified at 'src/lib' leaves the in-flight path set ['src/lib','src/types/multiplayer']. There U5a and U10 are exactFree=true but prefixFree=false: both own 'src/lib/multiplayer/server', nested inside U4's in-flight 'src/lib'. That is the double admission the old rule permits and the new rule refuses. The pin's --next fixture (FA local-verified at 'src/lib', FB planned at 'src/lib/multiplayer/server', FC planned at 'e2e') reproduces exactly that shape and is the case M3 kills.

nonClaims: --github depends on this machine's gh authentication and on GitHub being reachable. The green --github run is evidence about PR #1797 as GitHub answered it at 2026-09-17T16:30Z from this machine; it is not a hermetic check and it is opt-in for that reason. On a machine without gh the mode fails loudly (proved above) rather than passing.

The evidence mode checks EXISTENCE and SHAPE, not CONTENT. It proves a receipt file is on disk at the claimed path and that a product mainProof's runtime.playwright parses and, when red, carries one stated expectation per red row. It does not verify that the receipt describes the run it claims, that the counts inside it are true, that the expectedReds entries name the rows actually listed in failedRows, or that a proof was taken at all.

Receipts of blocked units are checked identically to any other - U2 (admission, red, local, review) and U12 (admission, red, local) are read the same way; being blocked buys no exemption. The mainProof parse rule is gated to ciClass 'product' only, so U0's docs-class mainProof (which carries no runtime block at all) is exempt by design.

The proof-line grammar implements exactly the three forms the unit names: '<label>: N failed / M passed', '<label>: N passed (...)' with the label optional, and '<label>: Tests: N passed, M total'. A jest summary that reports failures ('Tests: 3 failed, 59 passed, 62 total') is NOT in the grammar and would fail the parse; no receipt uses that shape today. Widening the grammar is a later unit's call, not this one's.

expectedReds is read from the mainProof RECEIPT FILE, at the top level or under runtime. The duplicate 'expectedReds' prose string inside units.json's U3 mainProof ledger entry (line 608) is not read and was not edited - units.json is outside this unit's edit set.
No claim is made about oxfmt formatting of the two .mjs files: .oxfmtignore excludes openspec/, so the formatter matched no target and the gate is inapplicable rather than green.

No build, no Playwright, no npm install/ci/prune was run; npm_config_dry_run=true was exported in every shell. No commit, push, stash or amend. The root checkout at E:/Projects/MekStation was never written to.
